name: StepsKit
tagline: Capture a workflow click by click and turn it into a shareable step-by-step guide or SOP.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The core mechanic is not mysterious: listen for clicks, grab a screenshot per click, crop around the cursor, name the button, emit an ordered document. An agent can get that working end to end in a weekend, and the output for your own runbooks will be genuinely useful. The pain is everything around it: browser extension permissions, capture reliability on canvas apps and iframes, redaction of anything sensitive that wanders into frame, and export formats that do not look like a school project. Hosted share links, team libraries and access control are a separate product you are not building. Verdict is a soft kinda: fine for personal SOPs, weak the moment other people need to read them on a URL you do not maintain.
coreLoopDIY: Records clicks in a browser tab, screenshots and crops each one, and compiles the sequence into an editable guide you can export as HTML, Markdown or PDF.
requirements: Chrome or another Chromium browser that can load an unpacked extension
whatYouLose: Hosted share links with permissions, so distributing a guide means sending a file
Automatic blur and redaction of emails, tokens and customer data that drift into a screenshot
Team libraries, versioning and 'who edited this SOP last' history
Polished export targets: branded PDF, Word, Confluence and Notion embeds
Capture that keeps working across odd apps: canvas UIs, iframes, native windows, multi-tab flows
moatNotes: The moat here is capture reliability and export that survives being sent to a coworker, not anything algorithmic.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because documentation tools live or die on whether the guide looks credible to the person receiving it, and because the tedium is in the last 10 percent: cropping consistently, redacting the account number, rewriting 'Click div.btn-primary' into 'Click Save', and getting a link that a contractor can open without installing anything. Teams also pay so the SOP library outlives the person who wrote it. A local build solves your own memory problem and none of the distribution problem.
notes: Great weekend project for personal runbooks, right up until someone asks for a link.
prompt:
Build "StepGuide", a local-first tool that records a browser workflow and turns it into a step-by-step guide.

Stack, no substitutions: a Chrome MV3 extension in plain TypeScript for capture, plus a Vite + React + TypeScript single-page editor. IndexedDB via Dexie for storage. No server, no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Capture (extension):
- Popup with Start, Stop, Discard, and a live step count.
- Content script listens for click and keydown-Enter on the active tab.
- On each event: capture the visible tab, record click coordinates, the element tag, its accessible name or inner text, and the page URL and title.
- Store steps in order in IndexedDB, images as blobs.
- Keyboard shortcut to start and stop recording.

Editor (SPA, opens from the popup):
- Library view of recordings; open one to edit.
- Per step: auto-generated instruction text like "Click Save", editable inline; reorder by drag; delete; duplicate.
- Image tools: auto-crop and zoom around the click point, a numbered circular marker at the click coordinates, manual crop, and rectangle blur for redaction (destructive, applied to the stored image).
- Guide-level title, intro paragraph, and step numbering.

Export:
- Standalone single-file HTML with base64 images.
- Markdown plus an images folder, zipped.
- Print stylesheet so browser print-to-PDF looks intentional.
- JSON import and export of the whole library.

Out of scope, do not build: hosted share links, sign-in, teams or permissions, capture outside the browser, video recording, AI text rewriting.

Deliver a README with load-unpacked install steps, dev commands, and a short honest note on which extension permissions are requested and why. No .env is needed because nothing leaves the machine; if you add anything network-bound later, read keys from .env and keep it off by default.
